issues.description: Method: Farm.addAnimal(Animal). The UML diagram in the problem statement declares addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean (problem_statement.md line 18). The textual task description in the same problem statement describes addAnimal(Animal a) only as "adds an animal to the list" with no return (problem_statement.md line 109). The provided solution implements addAnimal as public void addAnimal(Animal animal) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 23). The template Farm.java does not implement addAnimal and contains TODOs (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 3-6). This inconsistency (boolean vs void / unspecified) can confuse students whether to implement a boolean-returning method or a void method and may cause mismatches with tests or the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the mismatch between the UML and the implementation. Preferred fix (minimal disruption): update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal): void to match the task text, template, and solution. Alternatively, if a boolean return is required pedagogically, change the template and solution to implement public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) (returning true/false as appropriate) and update the textual task and any tests/Main usage accordingly. Ensure the problem statement text and UML are consistent.
